subject: Acme: OneTrust incremental CAIQ sync & API throttling mitigation
messages:
From: Emily Cho <e.cho@acmewidgets.com>
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: security-portal@acmewidgets.com
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OneTrust: incremental CAIQ sync & API throttling concerns

Hi Priya,

We're about to onboard Redwood's security profile into our OneTrust vendor portal and wanted to flag two requirements up front so we can avoid repeated follow-ups:

1) We want an incremental CAIQ/SCARF sync rather than a full manual upload every quarter. Ideally we pull a CAIQ-delta from Redwood's doc store via API or webhook to keep your profile fresh.

2) Our portal enforces aggressive API rate limits for third-party connectors during peak windows. If Redwood can provide a backoff-friendly retry strategy or a small window of elevated API rate (IP allowlist + token) for the initial seed, it will speed onboarding.

I've attached a CAIQ delta mapping (acme_caiq_delta_map.csv) that shows fields we expect to map automatically. Can your team confirm:
- Whether you can provide an S3-hosted CAIQ delta or an authenticated pull endpoint (we can provide a service account).
- A token rotation cadence you recommend for portal connectors.
- Any constraints around file naming/versioning we should follow.

Happy to set a short call if that's easier — we have 11–12 PT today.

Thanks,
Emily Cho
Manager, Vendor Risk & Compliance
Acme Widgets
Attachment: acme_caiq_delta_map.csv (CSV, 14 KB)

From: priya.natarajan@redwood.com
To: Emily Cho <e.cho@acmewidgets.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OneTrust: incremental CAIQ sync & API throttling concerns

Emily — thanks for the clear matrix and heads-up. We're happy to support an incremental CAIQ/CAI Q-delta flow into OneTrust. Quick answers and a proposed approach below:

- Delivery options: we can push deltas to an S3 bucket you control (pre-signed objects for each delta) or expose a scoped HTTP endpoint (token-protected) that OneTrust can call. For onboarding speed, S3 pre-signed objects are simplest.

- Rate limits: we'll implement an exponential backoff client on our side for retries. For the initial seed, we can coordinate an IP allowlist and a temporary higher token quota — please send the portal IPs/ASN and the service account email you plan to use.

- Token rotation: recommend a 30-day rotation for portal connectors; we can support automatic rotation notifications (email + webhook) to your security-portal address.

- Naming / versioning: we'll use a deterministic name pattern: redwood_caiq_delta_YYYYMMDD_vN.json and include a small manifest.csv in the same prefix (manifest lists file, checksum, created_at). Works with your sample?

Next steps (proposed):
1) Acme provides: service account email for S3 access OR OneTrust portal connector admin+IP allowlist.
2) Redwood will: upload 3 recent CAIQ deltas into the target S3 prefix and share presigned links; send the rotation plan doc.
3) Quick validation call (15 minutes) to confirm mapping fields in acme_caiq_delta_map.csv.

I attached a short proposal/plan (redwood-onetrust-sync-proposal.md) and an XLS mutual action plan (MAP-ACME-OneTrust-MAP-20270529.xlsx) so we can lock timelines. I'm copying Rishi (platform infra) for the token/rotation details and Ben (security ops) for audit/storage requirements.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Security Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-onetrust-sync-proposal.md (text, 3 KB); MAP-ACME-OneTrust-MAP-20270529.xlsx (XLSX, 18 KB)

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.com, Emily Cho <e.cho@acmewidgets.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OneTrust: incremental CAIQ sync & API throttling concerns

Looping in infra details. Short answers:

- S3 approach: we'll create a per-customer prefix under a hardened bucket (s3://redwood-infra/vendor-onboarding/acme-widgets/). Files will be written with server-side encryption (AES256) and ACLs scoped to the presigned object only. We'll provide presigned GETs valid for 48 hours for each delta pull.

- Token rotation: service accounts will be IAM keys scoped to a single upload role; we can rotate every 30 days and push a rotation notice to security-portal@acmewidgets.com and a webhook endpoint you configure. For emergency rotation we can support a 24-hour forced rotation window.

- Throttling: Redwood's connector respects Retry-After headers; we will also include a jittered exponential backoff. For the initial seed, if you allow our IPs (listed below) we can perform a batched seed during a maintenance window to avoid rate-limited backfill.

Proposed maintenance window for seed: Sun 2027-05-30 02:00–04:00 PT. IPs: 34.82.10.110, 34.82.10.111.

Ben — any audit logs or evidence artifacts you want us to include in the first upload (syslog, signed manifest) beyond the manifest.csv?

Onboarding checklist attached in the proposal — happy to stand up the S3 prefix tonight if Emily confirms S3 is OK.

—Rishi
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference

> > Emily — thanks for the clear matrix and heads-up. We're happy to support an incremental CAIQ/CAIQ-delta flow into OneTrust. Quick answers and a proposed approach below:
> >
> > - Delivery options: we can push deltas to an S3 bucket you control (pre-signed objects for each delta) or expose a scoped HTTP endpoint (token-protected) that OneTrust can call. For onboarding speed, S3 pre-signed objects are simplest.

From: priya.natarajan@redwood.com
To: Emily Cho <e.cho@acmewidgets.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OneTrust: incremental CAIQ sync & API throttling concerns

Emily — thanks, that plan works. Please confirm you want S3 presigned GETs to the prefix above and share the service account email (or provide OneTrust connector admin). Once we have that we will:

- Provision the prefix and post three delta files (with checksums).
- Share presigned links and the manifest.csv.
- Schedule the 15-minute validation call (I propose 11:30 PT today or 09:00 PT Monday).

Ben confirmed we'll include a signed manifest (GPG detached signature) and basic syslog snapshot for the seed. Rishi will coordinate the maintenance window if you want the batched seed.

If S3 is inconvenient, we can fall back to the token-protected endpoint, but S3 will be faster to validate on your side.

Thanks again — attaching the mutual action plan for signatures.

Priya Natarajan
Security Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Attachment: MAP-ACME-OneTrust-MAP-20270529.xlsx (XLSX, 18 KB)
